clue.text: Importance of parasites coming back, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: in tells us the turned parasites sit within the manner-of-speaking word

parts.note: diction is a way of speaking or enunciating

indicators.note: coming back tells us the parasites' word is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: nits are the eggs of lice, small parasites

explanation.surface: Someone muses on how much head lice matter, figuratively speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming back' turns NITS into STIN, which goes 'in' DICTION.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: distinction is eminence or importance, as in a person of distinction.

clue.text: Gives no warning to road users and couldn't care less

definitions.text: Gives no warning to road users
definitions.meaning: a driver who never sounds the horn literally fails to toot

explanation.surface: A careless driver who never sounds the horn and doesn't mind who gets hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: a hoot is a blast on a car horn.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to not care at all is to not give a damn, a fig, or a hoot.

clue.text: See 13
Where Oxonian may dream and breathe?

definitions.meaning: Oxford is the city of dreaming spires, so its resident dreams in a spire
to breathe in, or to breathe life into

explanation.surface: A question about where an Oxford student might sleep and draw breath.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as two words, IN SPIRE: Matthew Arnold called Oxford the 'city of dreaming spires'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to inspire originally means to draw air into the lungs.

clue.text: Change sides with Dr Who to become a ranch hand

indicators.note: to become signals the letters are turned into something else, rearranged
the sides of the word Change are its outermost letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The Time Lord swaps allegiance and takes up cattle ranching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sides' of 'Change' gives CE; mix CE with DRWHO, as 'to become' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A cattle herder is someone who works with livestock, like a hand on a ranch.

clue.text: One type of power about to switch

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the power word goes round the next piece

parts.note: solar energy is one kind of power
taken as written

explanation.surface: A single kind of electrical power is on the point of being changed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' looks like a verb in the surface but is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An isolator is an electrical switch that cuts a circuit off from its supply.

clue.text: Always a sudoku, possibly, for social harmony?

definitions.meaning: a number puzzle such as sudoku is at no time a word puzzle
peaceful relations with nobody having an angry exchange

explanation.surface: Someone claims a number puzzle is always a route to getting along with others.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes the answer literally: a sudoku is never a crossword, so 'Always' goes with 'never'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: people who never exchange an angry remark live in perfect harmony.

clue.text: Dump below?

parts.note: dump is slang for a trip to the toilet, and below hints at the lower body

explanation.surface: A terse question about leaving something down there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dump' looks like a rubbish tip, but it is crude slang for defecation, an act of the lower intestine.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphemism: the medical phrase for a passage of faeces through the gut.

clue.text: Funny man's rice pudding — second helping arrived, bowl first eaten

indicators.note: pudding suggests the rice is mashed and mixed up

parts.note: a second helping is more food

indicators.note: eaten means swallowed inside, so the bowl's letter goes into the arrival word

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the word bowl

explanation.surface: A comic describes a dessert: rice pudding, seconds served, and the bowl emptied first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pudding' scrambles RICE to ERIC; 'first' takes B from 'bowl', 'eaten' by CAME. ERIC MORECAMBE was a much-loved British comedian, partner of Ernie Wise; 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Eric Morecambe was a famous British comedian, half of a beloved TV double act.

clue.text: Heavy bones are not just visible with clothing removed

indicators.note: stripping each word of its outer letters leaves only the middles

explanation.surface: A remark that bones are seen only when you strip off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with clothing removed' strips the outer letters of each word: ONE, R, O, US.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a heavy duty or burden is an onerous one, demanding and oppressive.

clue.text: Any person yet to see whisky promoted?

indicators.note: promoted means moved up, so this letter shifts to the front of the word

parts.note: however means yet, nevertheless
W is whisky in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone asks who has not yet seen whisky being advertised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' moves the W of HOWEVER to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: whoever means whatever person, anyone at all.

clue.text: Ulster starts to expect witty improvisation in Irish comedian

indicators.note: in places the earlier pieces inside the Irish word

parts.note: Erse is the Irish Gaelic language
NI is Northern Ireland, often called Ulster

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: An Irish comic is expected to ad-lib wittily, starting in Ulster.
explanation.walkthrough: NI plus E, W, I ('starts to') goes 'in' ERSE. ERNIE WISE was the British comedian partnered with Eric Morecambe.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Ernie Wise was a famous British comic, the straight man of a TV double act.

clue.text: Captured by spies from the east saying you are made of gold

indicators.note: captured by means held within, so the sounded letters go inside the agency's letters
in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left, backwards

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency

indicators.note: saying signals the words are rendered as the letters that sound like them

parts.note: spoken quickly, the letters U and R sound like these two words

explanation.surface: Someone held by eastern spies is told they are made of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' turns CIA into AIC; 'saying' gives UR for 'you are', 'Captured by' AIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Auric is the adjective from Latin aurum, relating to or containing gold.

clue.text: Some great awful shop

indicators.note: awful suggests these letters are in a terrible mess, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumble about a dreadful store with a hint of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some great' looks like praise but it is the fodder, and 'awful' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A megastore is a very large shop, typically out of town.

clue.text: Boss had embraced sweetheart, given honest choice (not half)

indicators.note: embraced means held within, so the heart letter goes inside the word had

parts.note: taken as written
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter E

indicators.note: not half keeps only the first half of each of the two words honest and choice

explanation.surface: A boss hugged a lover and was offered an honest choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweetheart' is one word but works as 'heart of sweet', the middle letter E.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a head honcho is the person in charge, informally the big boss.

clue.text: One loses faith when a male part's not right …

indicators.note: not signals the right letter is left out of the gland

parts.note: the prostate is a gland found only in males

explanation.surface: A man loses his religion when something in his anatomy goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis ties this to the next clue, whose surface continues the story of male anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostate is someone who renounces a religious faith, a person who abandons belief.

clue.text: Six and half a dozen being the same not producing eggs

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
half a dozen is six, again VI
parity is equality, the state of being the same

explanation.surface: The saying 'six of one and half a dozen of the other' about two things being equal.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface echoes 'six of one, half a dozen of the other', meaning no difference.
explanation.definitionFit: Viviparity is bearing live young, as mammals do, instead of laying eggs.

clue.text: … and for performance, ultimately a male chemical

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of each of the two words

parts.note: a gent is a gentleman, a male

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a man takes a chemical to improve his performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives R and E, the last letters of 'for' and 'performance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reagent is a substance used to bring about a chemical reaction.

clue.text: Part of hospital in coma

indicators.note: in places the hospital letter within the stupor word

parts.note: a trance is a stupor, a state like a coma
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: A section of a hospital where patients lie in comas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts H inside TRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tranche is a portion or slice, especially of money or shares.

clue.text: Bird dived across the pond

definitions.meaning: a pigeon-like bird, symbol of peace
across the pond means in America, where the past tense of dive is often formed irregularly

explanation.surface: A bird plunged in over the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across the pond' is a common phrase for America, where 'dove' is a past tense of 'dive'.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is a familiar pigeon; the American past tense is a regional verb form.

clue.text: Intends to have different names in the same answer

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone plans to give several different names in one answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' hides the answer in 'same answer'; 'different names' is a second route, an anagram of NAMES, so the clue gives one answer two ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to mean something is to intend it.

clue.text: No pain or gain as ale is drunk

indicators.note: drunk signals the letters are tipsy and staggered into a new order

explanation.surface: A drinker's motto: no pain, no gain, as the beer goes down.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface twists 'no pain, no gain'; 'drunk' rearranges GAINASALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Analgesia is the absence of the sense of pain, or its relief by drugs.

clue.text: Grow up dear! That's not even cheese!

indicators.note: not even means keep the odd-numbered letters of the phrase and drop the rest

explanation.surface: A parent scolds a child to grow up, adding that something isn't even cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not even' takes the odd letters: G, O, U, D, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Gouda is a Dutch cheese named after its town of origin.

clue.text: Gas worried a very young person

parts.note: neon is a noble gas
ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried

explanation.surface: Gas leaks frightened a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: A neonate is a newborn infant, typically under four weeks old.

clue.text: Charge university student implicated in search

indicators.note: implicated in means caught up inside, so these letters go within the search word

parts.note: to comb is to search thoroughly
OU is the Open University, the UK's distance-learning university
L is a learner, as on a British learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A university student is charged after being caught up in a police search.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' looks like a criminal charge but is electrical. 'implicated in' puts OUL inside COMB, after its C.
explanation.definitionFit: The coulomb is the SI unit of electric charge.

clue.text: Dicky learned that in the West End

indicators.note: dicky means faulty or shaky, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Dicky picked something up in London's West End.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' looks like a name but means unsound, the anagram signal. The West End is London's theatre district.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatreland is the nickname for London's main district of theatres around Shaftesbury Avenue.
